messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — trying to wire the eval-runner artifacts into our ELK pipeline (logstash -> s3 indexer) so dashboards can show per-sample trace sizes and gzip ratios. Hit a weird CI failure: multipart upload succeeds but downstream indexer reports `unexpected end of file` when gunzipping some parts. Anyone seen stray gzip header truncation from the runner?

aj: Hmm saw related once. We chunk traces with gzip per-chunk and stream parts to S3. If multipart boundaries split a gzip stream incorrectly consumers will fail. Are we gzipping each part independently or the whole payload then chunking?

maria: We're gzipping per-sample batch before chunking. CI artifact uploader does: `gzip -c traces.jsonl | split -b 10M -d - traces.part.` then multipart upload. Logs show `zlib: unexpected EOF` in the indexer.

priya: Is the uploader doing any re-encode/compression on top of the provided parts? I recall the upload client has a `Content-Encoding` header toggle.

maria: Good call — the runner's s3 client was setting `Content-Encoding: gzip` on the whole object even though parts are pre-gzipped and merged server-side. Indexer tries to double-gunzip. But that should be harmless usually.

sam: Can you paste the exact error context from the indexer?

maria: Sure — snippet from indexer stderr: ```2026-11-12T04:23:15Z error: decompressing sample 4821: zlib: unexpected EOF; key=s3://eval-artifacts/2026/11/12/runner-2034567890-4821.part```

kevin: If parts are uploaded as separate objects then concatenated by some manifest reader, double-gzip could break depending on how concatenation is done. Concatenated gzip members are valid but some consumers expect a single member.

aj: Another angle: CI's `curl` client was retrying on 503 and appending partial bytes to an already-written part file in /tmp before the multipart commit, leading to corrupt part. We had a similar race in eng-infra last month.

priya: Did the CI artifact uploader surface retries in logs? We should look for `failed to write part` or `retrying part` entries around the timestamps (2034567905-2034567950).

maria: I dug logs — uploader shows `Retrying part 3 after 503` but then later `Multipart commit succeeded`. No explicit checksum verification per-part.

sam: Two mitigation ideas: 1) stop gzipping before splitting (gzip whole payload after concatenation), 2) add per-part CRC and verify before commit + enable S3 etag checks. Which is less invasive?

kevin: Option 2 is safer: compute per-part SHA256 locally, add `x-amz-meta-part-sha256` metadata, validate in the indexer. Also add CI job that replays a failing upload and validates decompression.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a small PR on the runner uploader to include per-part checksums and a `--verify` flag for CI. Also will add a quickfix in indexer to try concatenated-member tolerant gunzip (fallback) so we don't lose coverage retroactively.

priya: For the immediate CI belt-and-braces, can we add a post-upload `gzip -t` verification step in the runner CI job? That would catch corrupted gzip members before we register artifact as ready.

maria: Yes — plan: add `gzip -t` for each generated part artifact, then upload. If `gzip -t` fails -> abort and surface logs. I'll throw a small validation job into the eval-runner CI matrix.

devops-bot: Deploy task scheduled: uploader/2026-11-12/add-part-checksums -> staged to canary (eng-ml-ci) at 2034569000 UTC.

aj: One last note — metric side: we should record `artifact_part_verify_failures` and a histogram of `artifact_part_sizes_bytes` in the runner telemetry so we can alert on sudden changes when we flip compression modes.

maria: Excellent. I'll add telemetry tickets too. Putting the PR together now, will ping for review when ready :thumbsup:

kevin: Thanks — appreciate the speedy triage.
